qr-code.$description: QRCode. The two colours here are deliberately NOT theme-aware: they are scan optics, not styling. ISO/IEC 18004 readers expect dark modules on a light field, and many decoders do not try the inverted polarity, so the code keeps a light tile with dark modules in the dark theme too rather than inverting. Override them only with another dark-on-light pair of at least the same contrast.

foreground.$description: The modules. Theme-invariant black — maximum luminance contrast against the quiet zone in every theme, brand and forced-colors mode (the component opts out of forced-colour remapping).

background.$description: The quiet zone and the tile behind the modules. Theme-invariant white: in the dark theme this is the light tile that keeps the code scannable, which is the point — do not alias a theme-varying surface here.

corner.$description: The tile's corner. Only the quiet zone is rounded; the component drops the radius when the quiet zone is too thin to absorb it, so a corner never clips a finder pattern.

border.$description: A hairline around the tile, so a white code on a white card still shows where its quiet zone ends.
